notes: Derived edit with derived-belief and premise-route queries, chosen for transitivity: the second determinate query reaches Charles Darwin through 'is an ancestor of' (transitive), with the bridge 'Charles Darwin was the father of George Darwin', and is yes in both worlds while no before the edit. Derivability likely: the direct link is absent from Aage's side (0 'grandson of Christian Bohr', his article does not name the grandfather) and stated once in the lead of Christian Bohr's short article, while each premise is in the lead or birth sentence of a famous biography (evidence). Worlds: each lists the premise that gives way, the sibling side facts that go with it, and the dates; neither moves anyone outside the chain (George Darwin keeps his own children; in w2 Aage's father is one of them, whose own life is not otherwise asked). The fourth query uses a side fact: Harald stays Christian Bohr's son, so the brothers' full-sibling status turns on which premise gives way (fol: comparing the fathers of two people). Over-determination considered: Harald and Jenny as full siblings would re-derive P2; w1 makes them half-siblings, so P2 can still give way (as in people-replace-0003). R2: the Bohr surname hints at the premise answers, but no prompt contains its answer. George Darwin: implausible, clearly false, and dates allow both worlds. Near query (his Nobel year) is not moved. The ancestor query's 'no' before the edit rests on 'No member of the Darwin family was an ancestor of Aage Bohr', now a bridge with a check and a side fact that gives way in both worlds (it was unstated; formal check, FINDINGS C2).
